cards.text: Isaiah the prophet (Isaiah 37:2) just finished a burden against the Philistines (Isaiah 14:28-32). Now comes the next one: the burden against Moab, the nation that came from Lot's son Moab (Genesis 19:37). It opens with news about two Moab towns, Ar and Kir.

cards.question: Ar in Moab is ruined, and Kir in Moab is devastated. Each one is destroyed in a ___.

cards.text: Now the grief spreads from town to town. "Dibon goes up to its temple to weep at its high places."

cards.question: Moab wails over Nebo and over Medeba, and every head is shaved. What happens to every beard in Moab?

cards.text: In the streets, they wear sackcloth. On the rooftops and in the public squares, they all wail, falling down weeping.

cards.question: Moab wears sackcloth in the streets, and Heshbon and Elealeh cry out so loud they're heard as far as Jahaz. Through all this, Moab's soldiers stay calm and steady.
This is a burden against Moab. But as the speaker looks at Moab's ruin, what does the speaker's heart do?

cards.text: A heart crying out over Moab. You expected a victory party, and you got THAT. Meanwhile her fugitives flee as far as Zoar, weeping up the slope of Luhith on the road to Horonaim.

cards.question: As Moab's people flee, the waters of Nimrim are dried up.
Around Nimrim the grass is withered and the greenery is gone. What do Moab's people carry over the Brook of the Willows?

cards.text: Their outcry echoes to the border of Moab. Their wailing reaches all the way to Eglaim and Beer-elim.
The waters of Dimon are full of blood. Then the LORD, whose message this is (Isaiah 16:13), says, "I will bring more upon Dimon" and friend, it's not done yet.

cards.question: More is coming upon Dimon. What will come upon the fugitives of Moab and the remnant of the land?

cards.text: Then comes a command: "Send the tribute lambs to the ruler of the land" all the way from Sela in the desert.

cards.question: The tribute lambs are sent from Sela in the desert. Where are they sent to?

cards.text: The daughters of Moab are at the fords of the Arnon, like fluttering birds pushed out of the nest. I know that feeling, friend. My nest was a cookie counter, and I landed in a junk drawer.

cards.question: The daughters of Moab stand at the fords of the Arnon and plead. What do they ask for?
The prophecy looks ahead to when the oppressor has gone and destruction has ceased. Where will a throne be established in loving devotion?
A judge will sit on that throne in faithfulness, seeking ___ and hastening righteousness.

cards.text: Then the tone shifts again. "We have heard of Moab’s pomposity, his exceeding pride and conceit, his overflowing arrogance."

cards.question: Moab is full of pride and conceit. But the prophecy says his boasting is ___.

cards.text: Empty boasting, like the dead batteries I shared that drawer with, swearing EVERY day they still had a little charge left. So the prophecy says, "Therefore let Moab wail; let them wail together for Moab."

cards.question: The prophecy tells the utterly stricken to moan for the raisin cakes of Kir-hareseth, for the fields of Heshbon and the grapevines of Sibmah have withered.

cards.text: Those vines of Sibmah had reached as far as Jazer and spread toward the desert. Then the rulers of the nations trampled the choicest ones.

cards.question: The harvest is ruined and the best vines are trampled. How does the speaker respond to the vines of Sibmah?

cards.text: Joy is gone from the orchard, and no one sings or tramples the grapes anymore. Then the LORD, whose message this is (Isaiah 16:13), says, "I have put an end to the cheering."

cards.question: After all this, the speaker's heart still laments for Moab like a harp.

cards.text: Moab heads up to the high place, wears himself out, and goes into his sanctuary to pray.

cards.question: Moab wears himself out and prays in his sanctuary. What will it do for him?

answers.text: It will do him no good
It will turn the destroyer back
It will bring back the harvest

cards.text: This is the message the LORD spoke earlier concerning Moab. And now the LORD adds a timeline.

cards.question: The LORD says Moab's splendor will become an object of contempt in ___ years.

cards.text: Three years, "as a hired worker counts the years" and friend, NOBODY counts time closer than somebody on the clock at 4:59.

cards.question: When those three years are done, the people left in Moab will be many and strong.

findings.problem: The story card has three sentences: 'A heart crying out over Moab.' / 'You expected a victory party, and you got THAT.' / 'Meanwhile her fugitives flee...'

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: 'weeping up the slope of Luhith on the road to Horonaim' joins two separate clauses of Isaiah 15:5 into one place. The text says they ascend the slope of Luhith with weeping, and that they lament on the road to Horonaim. It never says the slope is on that road.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: Most of the stop's choice cards are discovery details that can't be reasoned out from the earlier cards: card 2 (destroyed in a night), card 4 (beards cut off), card 9 (waters of Nimrim dried up) and card 13 (a lion). That is 4 of its 7 choice cards, so informed guesses aren't the majority.

rule.text: A few of those are okay, as long as most choice cards are informed guesses.

findings.problem: Asking what happens to every beard (cut off, covered in ash or dipped in oil) is a detail guess about the wording of a prophetic line. It matches the Psalm 23 bad example ('What does He anoint David's head with?'). It doesn't ask about the movement or meaning of the lament.

rule.text: Ask about the movement and the meaning: what changes, what the picture is, why the speaker says what he says.

findings.problem: Stop 1's story cards are almost all flat narration with no Papa Dorin voice: card 1, card 3 (only a quote), card 5 and card 11. The only joke in the stop is the mild 'victory party' line on card 8. The stop reads like a plain summary, not laugh-out-loud Papa Dorin.

rule.text: If a line reads like a nice dad being pleasant, push it further.

findings.problem: The story card has three sentences: 'The daughters of Moab are at the fords...' / 'I know that feeling, friend.' / 'My nest was a cookie counter, and I landed in a junk drawer.'

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The true or false statement is a long, all-true restatement of Isaiah 16:7-8 (raisin cakes of Kir-hareseth, fields of Heshbon, vines of Sibmah). None of it was set up on an earlier card, and nothing in it can be reasoned out, so the pick is a coin flip.

rule.text: Before each choice card, Papa Dorin's story card gives enough context that the baker can reason their way to the answer.

findings.problem: 'The harvest is ruined' stretches Isaiah 16:9. The text says triumphant shouts have fallen silent over the summer fruit and the harvest. It never says the harvest is ruined.

rule.text: Don't stretch the text. Exaggerate only in his own jokes.

findings.problem: Card 12 calls the 'I' who weeps in Isaiah 16:9 'the speaker'. Card 13 then says 'Then the LORD ... says, "I have put an end to the cheering"' for 16:10, and card 14 goes back to 'the speaker' for 16:11. Together these imply a change of speaker between three back-to-back first-person lines. The text never shows that change.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: In this oracle, the first-person voice ('My heart cries out' 15:5, 'I will bring more' 15:9, 'I weep' 16:9, 'I have put an end' 16:10, 'my heart laments' 16:11) could be the prophet or the LORD. Isaiah 16:13 calls the whole thing 'the message that the LORD spoke.' The walkthrough names the LORD for some of these lines and 'the speaker' for others. papa-dorin.md says to name who it is before quoting an 'I', but the Scripture rules say to leave open what the text leaves open.
findings.question: When a prophetic passage speaks as 'I' and the text doesn't say whether it's the prophet or the LORD, should Papa Dorin name a speaker (and if so, which one), or always say 'the speaker' and leave it open?
